quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: A police officer pulls you over. Should you exit your vehicle and quickly approach the officer's car?
questions.explanation: Stay in your vehicle when stopped by police. Keep both hands visible on the steering wheel.

questions.question: You are stopped at a railroad crossing for a train. After the train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not move until all gates are raised and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
questions.explanation: A round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. It appears a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator gets stuck while you are driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock.
questions.explanation: A stuck accelerator will keep your vehicle moving even if you remove your foot from the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully, moving it only enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: Talking or texting on your phone while driving does not significantly increase your risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Using your phone while driving is a distraction that increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at the same speed.
One lane is traveling faster than another.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen more often when one driver travels faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases crash risk. Driving slower than traffic also increases risk because of rear-end collisions or other drivers swerving to avoid you.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded roads near trees or buildings. These areas freeze first and dry last.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows a divided highway ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads with a median between them. Stay on your right side.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane but there is no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you, then continue.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: The distance from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum legal height for vehicles in this state.
The maximum width for vehicles on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance sign. It shows how much space is between the road and a bridge or overpass (in this case, 12 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: When bad weather or darkness requires you to turn on your lights:
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Do not stay in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.
Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.
Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, check that your tires have good tread and are inflated correctly. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: You must use your low beams when you are:
questions.explanation: Use your low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and cause glare. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you (within posted speed limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot crash into each other. Most multi-vehicle crashes happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they contradict traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly to get back visibility. Return to your lane only when you can see both of the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you stay in your lane, control your vehicle, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This sign is a regulation sign. It means right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first when turning left. Only complete your turn when the intersection is clear and the signal allows it.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, do not panic. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to let the vehicle slow down. Apply the brakes gently when it is safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What must drivers allow for when driving near heavy trucks?

options.text: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
Heavy trucks can stop in a shorter distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: When driving near heavy trucks, allow extra space because trucks need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see around the truck.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when driving behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Move your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly. Rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Press the brakes gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Which statement about drinking and driving is true?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes poor.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and often makes you take more risks.

questions.question: Speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.
questions.explanation: On the highway, stay far behind the vehicle in front of you. As your speed increases, the distance needed to stop also increases.

questions.question: Why is it important to look far ahead on the highway?

options.text: It helps you keep up with traffic.
It reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
It allows you to spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead to avoid last-minute braking or turning. By watching ahead and being ready to stop or change lanes, you drive safer, save fuel, and help traffic flow smoothly.

questions.question: What must you do when entering a street from a driveway?

options.text: Drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Honk your horn so others know to get out of your way.
Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians crossing. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Failing to stop is against the law.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. Most tires can push water away up to 35 mph. When you go faster than 35 mph, tires cannot move the water away as well. Your tires may lose grip on the road and slide over the water like water skis.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing:

options.text: As long as an approaching train is not too close.
If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
If you first look carefully in both directions.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: If worried, nervous, angry, or crying, a driver:

options.text: Will drive no differently than if thinking more clearly.
Can drive faster because they are more aware.
Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your driving. Worry, anger, crying, or sadness can distract you because your mind is on other things. Calm down and focus on driving before you start the car.

questions.question: This sign is used to prevent:

options.text: Wrong-direction entrances on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong-direction entrances on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic flows one way only. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop your vehicle immediately and block their path.
Do everything you can to clear a path for the emergency vehicle.
Signal to the emergency vehicle when it is safe for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear a path for the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near, you must clear a path for it. If safe, pull your car to the side of the road to give the emergency vehicle room to pass.
